# `starhermit:storage`

Engine **1.41.0** (host API 1.41), the latest release. Generated from the release's `starhermit.d.ts`; `starhermit types` writes the same file into your game. [All modules](index.md).

```ts
import { … } from "starhermit:storage";
```

Needs the manifest's `storage` capability: without it every call throws `NotAllowedError`. Storage is the game's own (no other game or package can read it), kept per game, player and environment.

### KeyValueStorage

*interface*

Game-private key/value storage on this device. A write is seen by every read at once and reaches the disk atomically as the frame (or lifecycle call) ends, so a key set many times a frame is written once. Keys are 1–120 bytes of UTF-8 text; a value is at most `engine.limits.storage_key_kib` (1 MiB); the game holds at most `storage_mib` (64 MiB), each key counted in whole 4 KiB blocks, and at most 4,096 keys; and it writes at most 16 MiB at once, refilled at 4 MiB a second (keys counted in whole blocks, rewrites of a key in the same frame free). Past any of these a write throws a RangeError and changes nothing.

```ts
export interface KeyValueStorage { … }
```

- `get(key: string): Uint8Array | null;`
- `getText(key: string): string | null;`

- `getJson(key: string): JsonValue | null;`

  Parses what `setJson` wrote; other contents throw a SyntaxError.

- `set(key: string, value: string | Uint8Array | ArrayBuffer): void;`
- `setJson(key: string, value: JsonValue): void;`

- `remove(key: string): boolean;`

  Whether the key existed.

- `keys(): string[];`
- `usage(): { readonly bytes: number; readonly keys: number; readonly quotaBytes: number; readonly maxKeys: number };`

### LocalStorage

*interface*

The Web Storage interface (`localStorage`'s `Storage`) over \{@link storage\} (since API\_MINOR 37, `LOCAL_STORAGE_MINOR`; undefined for games declaring an older `engine.minor`), for a browser build's shared scripts (`js/*.js`) that keep their records in `localStorage`. It is a view of the same keys: `getItem(key)` is `storage.getText(key)`, `setItem` is `storage.set` with text, so what one writes the other reads, with storage's persistence (a write reaches the disk as the frame ends), limits and capability (without `storage` in the manifest's capabilities every call throws `NotAllowedError`). As Web Storage, keys and values are converted to strings (`setItem("n", 1)` stores `"1"`, a Symbol is a TypeError), too few arguments are a TypeError, and a write past storage's limits (a value over 1 MiB, the game's quota or its key count) throws an Error named `QuotaExceededError` and changes nothing; one past storage's write rate (16 MiB at once, 4 MiB a second) throws a RangeError, as `storage.set` does, and changes nothing. `removeItem` and `clear()` never throw (`clear()` removes every key of `storage` at once). Keys and values keep every UTF-16 code unit: a lone surrogate, and U+FFFF, are stored as U+FFFF and the unit's four hex digits (other text as it is, so `storage.getText` reads it). Keys are storage's: a key that is not 1–120 bytes of text (so stored) without control characters is never set (`getItem` gives null, `removeItem` does nothing, `setItem` throws a TypeError). `key(i)` and `length` follow `storage.keys()` (the keys in order of their UTF-8 bytes). A key holding bytes that are not UTF-8 throws a TypeError from `getItem`, as from `getText`. The object and its prototype are frozen: items are read and written through the methods only (no `localStorage.name` properties).

```ts
export interface LocalStorage { … }
```

- `readonly length: number;`
- `key(index: number): string | null;`
- `getItem(key: string): string | null;`
- `setItem(key: string, value: string): void;`
- `removeItem(key: string): void;`
- `clear(): void;`

### localStorage

*const*

```ts
export const localStorage: LocalStorage;
```

### installLocalStorage

*function*

```ts
export function installLocalStorage(): LocalStorage;
```

Makes \{@link localStorage\} the global `localStorage` (since API\_MINOR 37, `LOCAL_STORAGE_MINOR`) and returns it, so a classic script loaded after (`loadClassic`) reads and writes the device's storage as it did the browser's. Opt-in, as the global is the browser build's name: the engine defines no `localStorage` of its own (a game may still assign its own), and the browser's game worker has none either. Call it before the scripts that read the global run (at the top of the module imported first).

### GameSettings

*interface*

The game's own settings (difficulty, camera options), kept with the player's engine settings: on this device, and in the player's account when signed in (the platform's per-game settings, as `game.<key>`: keys match `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,128}`, those past 123 characters stay on the device, within the platform's key and byte limits). The account is read once as the session starts; its values arrive through `onChange` for keys the game did not set since, and edits go up 800 ms after the last. Engine settings (audio, graphics, bindings) are the runtime's and not visible here.

```ts
export interface GameSettings { … }
```

- `get(key: string): JsonValue | undefined;`

- `set(key: string, value: JsonValue): void;`

  Throws a TypeError for an invalid key, RangeError past the limits.

- `delete(key: string): void;`
- `keys(): string[];`

- `onChange(listener: (key: string, value: JsonValue | undefined) => void): Unsubscribe;`

  Changes from another device or from the account arriving.

- `legacyKeys(): string[] | null;`

  Legacy settings (since API\_MINOR 8): the account's settings for this game under keys that are neither the game's (`game.`) nor the engine's (`sh.`, `graphics.`), as a build of the game from before the engine (the JS SDK's `setSetting`) wrote them. Their keys as the session's read found them, or null until that read landed (signed out, offline, or the read failed). Read only: the game migrates them and removes them.

- `legacy(key: string): JsonValue | undefined;`

  A legacy setting's value (undefined when absent or not read yet). A `game.`, `sh.` or `graphics.` key, or one outside `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,128}`, throws a TypeError.

- `removeLegacy(key: string): boolean;`

  Removes a legacy setting from the account (it goes up with the game's edits, 800 ms after the last); whether it was there. Keys as `legacy`.

- `onLegacy(listener: () => void): Unsubscribe;`

  The legacy settings were read (once a session, after sign-in).

### ForeignSave

*interface*

A save in the account's slot that the engine did not write (since API\_MINOR 8): a build of the game from before the engine saved it (the JS SDK's `writeSave`, a ZIP archive with one `save.json`), or anything else put there through the platform's API.

```ts
export interface ForeignSave { … }
```

- `readonly text: string | null;`

  Its text: the archive's `save.json` (or its only file) as the JS SDK's `loadSave` reads it, or else the slot's bytes, as UTF-8; null when that is not UTF-8 text (a file expands to at most 16 MiB).

- `readonly bytes: Uint8Array;`

  The slot's bytes, byte for byte as the old build stored them (at most 10 MiB): a build that kept raw gzip there (`text` is then null) reads as `new TextDecoder().decode(decompress(bytes, "gzip"))`.

### CloudSave

*interface*

The game's save: one per game and player, kept on the device and, when signed in, synced to the account (the platform's cloud save slot of the game: read once signed in, then uploads conditional on the version they were based on, debounced 2 s, at most every 30 s, queued while offline; a failed read blocks uploads, local play goes on). At most 10 MiB of JSON (RangeError). The previous save is kept as a recovery checkpoint. The account's save replacing the device's (another device saved last) shows in `load()`; `onStatus` hears the change.

```ts
export interface CloudSave { … }
```

- `load(): Save | null;`

  The current save, or null when there is none (yet).

- `previous(): Save | null;`

  The save before the current one.

- `save(data: JsonValue, options?: { schema?: number; replaceForeign?: boolean }): void;`

  Replaces the save; it is written to the device at once. `replaceForeign` (since API\_MINOR 8): this save also replaces the account's foreign save the game was shown (`foreign()`), uploaded at once and only if the slot still holds that version; otherwise (or without one) it is an ordinary save.

- `foreign(): ForeignSave | null;`

  The account's slot holds a save the engine did not write (since API\_MINOR 8): it is never adopted or overwritten by itself. While it is there `state()` is `"foreign"` and `status()` `"pending"`: saves stay on the device and none is uploaded until the game migrates it and saves with `replaceForeign`. Null when there is none, signed out, offline, or until the slot was read (`onStatus` hears `"foreign"` once this has it). If the old build saves again before the replacement lands, the newer one is shown here instead (the replacement stays on the device); if another device replaced it first, `onConflict` hears both engine saves. The slot is read again each session, never kept on the device.

- `status(): SaveStatus;`
- `state(): SyncState;`

- `flush(): Promise<SaveStatus>;`

  Writes pending changes now (resolves when stored or queued).

- `onConflict(listener: (local: Save, remote: Save) => Resolution | Promise<Resolution>): Unsubscribe;`

  The account holds a different save than this device: resolve it (until then the account's copy is not overwritten). The first listener that answers resolves; `local` is null when this device had none.

- `onStatus(listener: (status: SaveStatus, state: SyncState) => void): Unsubscribe;`
